auth.safeNotice: The safe variant sends the same payload so you can verify that the backend blocks injection.
auth.unsafeNotice: The unsafe variant intentionally has an authentication flaw. Use synthetic data for this demonstration.

lab.pageDescription: Compare security outcomes and review authentication events.
lab.safeExplanation: The query only finds the username; the password is independently verified with scrypt.
lab.unsafeSqlExplanation: The unsafe variant concatenates input into SQL. A payload string can alter the syntax and query condition to bypass password verification.
lab.unsafeMongoExplanation: The unsafe variant passes input directly into the query. An operator object can replace the password comparison; ordinary strings are still compared as values.
lab.rejectedExplanation: Validation blocked the request before the authentication query. The session and audit log may still use the database.
lab.appDescription: Application-flow description; this is not a database trace.
lab.emptyDiagnostic: Choose a payload and send the request. The result comes from the real database, not a browser-side simulation.

ownership.title: Request read access
ownership.instruction: Open the request list as a student. It should show only that account's requests. The API test confirms another student's request returns HTTP 403.

admin.title: Admin actions and profile edits
admin.instruction: Update a request as an administrator, then reopen it as its owner to see the new status. API tests confirm students cannot change status, create accounts, or change their role through the profile.

session.title: Sessions and account locking
session.instruction: Open another variant to check session isolation. API tests confirm an old session loses access after logout or when its account is locked.

apostrophe.title: Valid text with an apostrophe
apostrophe.instruction: Save and reopen a title such as Request from O'Connor. Confirm that the apostrophe is preserved.

disclosure.title: Out-of-scope record disclosure
disclosure.request: View a request from Group A.
disclosure.defense: Scope results to the signed-in account and return only the fields needed for display.
disclosure.unsafe: The response contains three records, including two from Group B.
disclosure.safe: The response contains only one record from Group A.

targeted-update.title: Out-of-scope record update
targeted-update.defense: Check authorization for each record and constrain the update scope.
targeted-update.unsafe: One record was changed, but it was Group B's M-02.

bulk-update.title: Unexpected bulk update
bulk-update.defense: Use a fixed condition based on the ID and owner. Check affected rows before committing the transaction.

bulk-delete.title: Deleting multiple records
bulk-delete.defense: Limit the action by permission and record ID. Use a transaction so it can be rolled back if more rows than expected are affected.
bulk-delete.safe: One record was deleted; two remain.

table-loss.title: Dropping a table or collection
table-loss.defense: Give schema-management access to a separate account. The application account should have only the data permissions it needs.
table-loss.unsafe: The next read fails because the illustrative table or collection is gone.
table-loss.safe: The table or collection remains available and returns three records.

privilege.title: Changing privileges through a data update
privilege.request: Change the display name of a sample account.
privilege.defense: Accept only permitted profile fields. Role changes require a separate server-side authorization check.
privilege.unsafe: Both the name and role changed. The sample account now has administrator access.

error-details.title: Information disclosed in error messages
error-details.request: Submit a value with an invalid format.
error-details.defense: Return a concise error to the user. Keep necessary details in access-controlled logs.
error-details.unsafe: The message reveals an internal table name and field in this hypothetical example.
error-details.safe: The message only says that the submitted data is invalid.

response-difference.title: Information leaked through different responses
response-difference.request: Compare responses for two hypothetical cases.
response-difference.defense: Keep public responses consistent when differences could disclose protected information.
response-difference.unsafe: Different responses may reveal a property without returning its value.
response-difference.safe: Both responses use the same public message.

authentication.title: Authentication with an incorrect password
authentication.request: Attempt to sign in with an incorrect password.
authentication.defense: Find the account with a constrained query, then verify the password independently. Valid passwords must still work.
authentication.unsafe: The hypothetical application creates a session despite invalid credentials.
authentication.safe: The server rejects the sign-in and does not create a session.

mongo-types.title: Data types in MongoDB authentication
mongo-types.request: Compare an object, JSON string, array, null, number, and correct password.
mongo-types.defense: Accept passwords only as strings. Reject invalid types before looking up credentials.
mongo-types.unsafe: In this hypothetical example, an object is treated as a query condition and the application creates a session.
mongo-types.safe: Objects, arrays, null, and numbers are blocked before the query. Invalid JSON strings return 401; a correct password returns 200.

ticket-ownership.title: Student request ownership
ticket-ownership.request: Have a Group A student open their own request, then compare it with a Group B request.
ticket-ownership.defense: Check ownership on the server for every request.
ticket-ownership.unsafe: The hypothetical missing check returns a Group B request too.
ticket-ownership.safe: The Group B request is denied. The student's own request still returns HTTP 200.

role-boundaries.title: Restricted actions and role fields
role-boundaries.request: Compare a student's ability to change status, create accounts, and update a profile.
role-boundaries.defense: Check roles on the server and accept only permitted profile fields.
role-boundaries.unsafe: The hypothetical missing check permits an admin-only action or accepts a role change through the profile.

session-boundaries.title: Session isolation, logout, and account locking
session-boundaries.request: Compare profile access on another variant, after logout, and while the account is locked.
session-boundaries.defense: Use a separate cookie per variant, destroy sessions on logout, and check account status on every data request.
session-boundaries.unsafe: The hypothetical missing check accepts an old session or one from another variant.
session-boundaries.safe: The server requires a valid session for the current variant and an active account.

legitimate-apostrophe.title: Valid text containing an apostrophe
legitimate-apostrophe.request: Save and reopen a request titled Request from O'Connor.
legitimate-apostrophe.defense: Pass data through parameters or a fixed data field so the apostrophe is preserved.
legitimate-apostrophe.unsafe: The hypothetical over-filter rejects a valid title.
legitimate-apostrophe.safe: The request is saved and read back unchanged.
